chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Qarawī, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Ismāʿīl al-Jabalī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning:
the salat (prayer) of the two Eids, he said:

He pronounces one takbīr with which he opens the salat (prayer), then recites Umm al-Kitāb and a surah, then pronounces five takbīrs, performing qunūt between them, then pronounces one takbīr and bows with it. Then he stands and recites Umm al-Qurʾān and a surah.
He recites in the first: “Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High,” and in the second: “By the sun and its morning brightness.”
Then he pronounces four takbīrs, performing qunūt between them, then he bows with the fifth.

key_terms.أُمَّ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, the Opening of the Book
key_terms.سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى: the surah recited in the first rakʿah
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the salat (prayer) of the two Eids
key_terms.وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا: the surah recited in the second rakʿah
key_terms.يَقْنُتُ: he performs qunūt, a supplicatory standing

ai.seo_question: How is the Eid salat (prayer) performed according to this hadith from al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of performing the salat (prayer) of the two Eids, detailing the sequence of takbīrs, recitation, qunūt, and rukūʿ. It also specifies the surahs to be recited in the first and second rakʿahs, making it an important narration in the fiqh of Eid prayer.
